newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks end higher but doubts remain about rally.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks end higher but doubts remain about rally.

text.p: ** UK shares end higher, boosted by continued Wall Street
strength as well as firm gilts.
** FTSE within striking distance of all-time record levels
but analysts warn new highs may not be set until after
market has suffered a modest downward correction.
Trading volume was a modest 733 million shares by 1630 GMT, continuing to reflect the market's general unease over the both the FTSE and the Dow's current near-record levels, dealers said.
The Dow industrials average, which surged 82 points on Monday after dropping 140 points the previous week, was up 28 points by the London close.
U.S. blue chips have risen by nearly 30 percent this year, prompting fears that a substantial correction may not be too far away.
Whereas a Dow slippage, if it comes, could be quite severe, analysts believed the FTSE may not suffer a drastic decline.
They noted that UK blue chips have only risen around nine percent, or one-third of the Dow's advance this year.

"I really wouldn't get too worried about the FTSE coming down. It's due for a bit of a correction but its long-term uptrend still appears to be intact," said Dave Sneddon technical analyst at Credit Suisse.

In the short-term, FTSE appears to have solid support at around 3,900, a level that has not been breached since early September. "The 3,892 to 3,900 level is really the key support," Sneddon said. "If that level fails, the FTSE could fall all the way back to around 3,600 -- about where it started the year".

The FTSE 100 has been trading in a 200-point range since setting a record closing level of 4,073.1 on October 21. The most recent assault on that record was last week -- a week that ended with an 88-point plunge on "Grey Friday".
Sneddon believes the FTSE will struggle in the near-term to break out above the 4,060-4,070 level but even if a new record is set over the next few days he sees a limited upside at around 4,120.
"I would certainly like to see 4,120 taken out before I will be confident that we won't see a correction," he said. "But I really don't see that (4,120 level) being breached."

Another robust performance by UK gilts lent support to share prices, dealers said. The March gilt future outperformed both the March U.S. T-bond and the March bund, thanks to a stronger sterling and expectations that UK base rates will remain steady.
UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke is not expected to signal a rate rise after Wednesday's monetary meeting with Bank of England governor Eddie George.
Clarke boosted market hopes for steady rates after telling a British parliamentary committee late Monday that wage and commodities inflation pressures were very low.
The March gilt future ended 18/32 higher at 110-5/32.

B.A.T Industries, up 12p at 488-1/2, was the most active FTSE 100 stock of the session, with over 23 million shares changing hands by 1630 GMT. The tobacco giant continued to benefit from talk it may be considering a demerger.

Barclays touched a record trading high of 10.42 stg before closing at 10.34-1/2 stg, up 12p on the day. The British banking group lifted after a "buy" recommendation from analysts at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
Reed International's, down 15p to 10.68 stg, continued to suffer from the hangover induced by last week's profit downgrades.
-- Dale Faulken, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
